news.h: Maybulk to expand into industrial property business with Klang land buy
news.body: Transportation and logistics group Maybulk Bhd has proposed to buy a freehold industrial property in Bandar Bukit Raja, Klang for RM35.5m cash. The property comprises 8,346 sq m of land together with a single-storey industrial building, an annexed office and a warehouse block, the group said in an exchange filing. Maybulk said the acquisition forms part of its push into the industrial property business to diversify revenue and reduce reliance on its core shipping and storage operations. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The price works out at about RM4,250 a square metre, or roughly RM395 a square foot, on the item's own two figures - RM35.5m across 8,346 sq m, computed here. That is not a land price: it buys the land plus a single-storey industrial building, an annexed office and a warehouse block, and the item gives no split between them, no built-up area and no valuation, so the land component cannot be separated from the buildings.

This board holds one comparable and it is an imperfect one. On 4 September, Orgabio agreed to pay RM11.3m for 5,263 sq m of freehold industrial land at Jalan Bangi, Semenyih - about RM2,150 a square metre, or roughly RM200 a square foot, and recorded here at the time. Maybulk is paying about 1.98 times that per square metre, computed here, but Orgabio was buying bare land to build a warehouse on while Maybulk is buying land with buildings already standing. The two are the same asset class in different states; the comparison is drawn here and is not like-for-like.

Bandar Bukit Raja is a township this board has already carried, from the other end of the development chain. On 17 September it recorded PTT Synergy's RM83.3m earthworks contract from Sime Darby Property for multiple packages in Phase 1 of Bandar Bukit Raja Stage 4, also in Klang, with possession from 29 September 2026. Today a listed shipping group is buying completed industrial product in the same township. Neither item mentions the other; the pairing is made here, and the item does not say whether Maybulk's property sits within the Sime Darby Property masterplan.

The strategic claim is the whole item and none of it is quantified. The stated purpose is to diversify revenue and reduce reliance on core shipping and storage operations - but no current revenue split, no rental yield, no tenant, no lease term, no completion date and no target contribution from the new segment appears. A single RM35.5m cash purchase is disclosed; a business line is asserted.

This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Maybulk, and the 23 September bundle is a single IHH Healthcare Company Update, so no report in this edition covers shipping, logistics or industrial property. The nearest shipping name in this board's Kenanga record is MISC, last carried as a Results Note on 28 August and named on 17 September as Kenanga's preferred way to own oil and gas ahead of high-beta PCHEM - a tanker-rate story, not a bulk-carrier or property one.

news.h: OGX Group ventures into renewable energy, targets data centre market
news.body: OGX Group Bhd has ventured into the renewable energy (RE) industry, targeting opportunities in Malaysia's growing data centre market through battery energy storage systems (BESS). The information technology infrastructure solutions provider said its wholly owned subsidiary OGX Green Tech Sdn Bhd will spearhead the new business. The group said Zhejiang Hyxi Technology Co Ltd (HYXI), a China-based energy storage and inverter specialist with a presence across Europe, has appointed OGX Green Tech as an authorised distributor to market, distribute and sell HYXI's products in Malaysia. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: What was signed is a distributorship, not a project, and the item contains no figure of any kind. OGX Green Tech has been appointed an authorised distributor for HYXI's products in Malaysia - no contract value, no minimum volume, no exclusivity, no term, no capital commitment, no margin and no revenue target. Nothing here can be sized, annualised or tracked in a later edition.

The gap between what the company does and what it is now selling is the part worth noting. OGX is described as an information technology infrastructure solutions provider, and the counterparty is a China-based energy storage and inverter specialist. Between them they supply hardware; neither is described as developing, owning or operating a project, so this is a channel arrangement into the data centre buildout rather than participation in it.

It is the second battery-storage item this board has carried in a month and both are distribution deals with foreign partners. On 11 September, Cape EMS partnered Singapore-based Helios PV to distribute Malaysian-assembled residential BESS in Europe and Asia-Pacific, using its Senai plant. That one exports Malaysian-assembled product outward; this one imports Chinese product inward for the domestic data centre market. Opposite directions on the same technology; the grouping is made here.

Kenanga's own sizing of the opportunity this is aimed at is on this board, and it does not cover storage. Its 21 September Renewable Energy Sector Update puts Malaysia's secured data centre maximum demand at about 8.35GW today against a PETRA projection of about 21GW by 2040, and derives roughly RM19bn of addressable work from the incremental demand at 30% renewable usage - but that arithmetic is solar EPCC, at about RM5m per MW, and the c.RM16bn companion figure is CRESS solar capacity already registered with the Single Buyer. Storage is not in either number, so this board holds no Kenanga estimate against which a BESS distributorship could be measured. That limitation is identified here.

This board holds no Kenanga coverage of OGX Group, and the 23 September bundle - one healthcare Company Update - carries no renewable energy, utilities or technology report. Kenanga's named RE exposures on this board are SLVEST, whose target was raised to RM3.76 from RM3.36 and which it called the preferred CRESS exposure on 21 September, and SAMAIDEN at RM2.90 from RM2.50.

news.h: Carimin makes Sealink an associate by upping stake to 25.3%
news.body: Carimin Petroleum Bhd has made Sealink International Bhd an associate company after increasing its Sealink stake to 25.3%. This development comes about three months after Carimin's proposal to take Sealink private lapsed. The oil and gas services provider said it acquired 29.1m Sealink shares at 34 sen apiece via direct business transactions between Sept 18 and Sept 22 for RM9.9m. This increased Carimin's shareholding in Sealink from 19.5% to 25.3%, maintaining its position as Sealink's largest shareholder. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The figures reconcile and they imply a share count the item never prints. 29.1m shares at 34 sen is RM9.894m, which is the RM9.9m stated. The stake moved 5.8 percentage points, from 19.5% to 25.3%, so 29.1m shares represent 5.8% of Sealink - putting the issued base at about 502m shares, and Carimin's resulting holding at about 127m shares. All three steps computed here; none appears in the item.

Crossing 20% is the substance, and it changes the accounting rather than the control. At 25.3% with significant influence Sealink becomes an associate, so Carimin equity-accounts its share of Sealink's results instead of recognising dividends only. The item gives no Sealink earnings figure, no net asset value and no goodwill treatment, so the effect on Carimin's profit and loss cannot be established from the retrieved source.

It is a second approach at a target the first approach failed to secure. Carimin's proposal to take Sealink private lapsed about three months ago; it has now bought a further 5.8% in the open market over five days, from 18 to 22 September, via direct business transactions. The item does not state the lapsed offer price, so whether 34 sen is above or below what Carimin was previously willing to pay cannot be established here.

Direct business transactions rather than on-market purchases is the operative detail. They are negotiated off-market crossings, so the 34 sen is a bilateral price with an unnamed counterparty, not necessarily a market-clearing one - and the item gives no market price for Sealink, which appears in none of this edition's top-volume, top-gainer or top-loser tables.

This board holds no Kenanga coverage of either Carimin or Sealink, and the 23 September bundle contains no oil and gas report. Kenanga's oil and gas coverage on this board runs through KEYFIELD (18 September), UZMA (1 September), DAYANG and VELESTO (24 August), ARMADA, WASCO and MISC (28 August), and the Oil & Gas Sector Update of 1 September. The nearest prior consolidation item is the reported MISC-led consortium offer for Yinson, carried on 28 August.

news.h: MMAG proposes RM130.0m capital reduction to pare accumulated losses
news.body: Loss-making MMAG Holdings Bhd, a company which counts NexG Bhd as a substantial shareholder, has proposed a RM130.0m share capital reduction to wipe out part of the company's accumulated losses. NexG is the company's second largest shareholder with a 9.9% stake, while Future Star Sdn Bhd is its largest shareholder with a 19.9% interest. The exercise will allow the ACE Market-listed company to eliminate accumulated losses and better reflect the value of its underlying assets, thereby strengthening the group's financial position and profile with its bankers, customers, suppliers, investors and other stakeholders. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: It is the second share capital reduction in two consecutive editions and the less informative of the two. Yesterday this board carried Straits Energy Resources eliminating RM90.0m of losses, and that item printed every input - RM39.2m of group accumulated losses at 30 June 2026, RM50.8m of resulting retained earnings, RM101.9m at company level leaving RM11.9m - and reconciled exactly in both directions. Today's item says only that RM130.0m will wipe out 'part of' the accumulated losses, with no balance stated, so the residual deficit cannot be computed at all.

The mechanics are the same and they move no cash. A share capital reduction transfers value from share capital to accumulated losses or retained earnings; no money enters the company, no borrowing is repaid and no asset changes hands. What the word 'part' establishes is that MMAG's accumulated losses exceed RM130.0m - which is the only inference the item supports, and it is drawn here.

The stated rationale is presentational rather than financial, and unusually explicit about audience. The exercise will 'better reflect the value of its underlying assets, thereby strengthening the group's financial position and profile with its bankers, customers, suppliers, investors and other stakeholders'. Dividends are not mentioned - which is the difference from yesterday's item, where restoring distributable reserves was the readable purpose.

The shareholder structure is given and it is unusually flat for an ACE Market company. Future Star Sdn Bhd holds 19.9% and NexG Bhd 9.9%, together 29.8%, computed here - so neither is close to a majority, and the item names no other holder, no board representation and no relationship between the two. NexG is described as a substantial shareholder and nothing more.

This board holds no Kenanga coverage of MMAG Holdings or NexG, and the 23 September bundle contains a single report - an IHH Healthcare Company Update - so there is no read-across in this edition. Capital-restructuring items are now a running theme here: Pimpinan Ehsan's capital reduction and repayment on delisting (10 September), Excel Force's RM11.0m placement and Straits Energy's RM90.0m reduction (22 September), and this.

news.h: Forced auction of Country Heights land cancelled due to lack of bidders
news.body: A forced auction of Country Heights Holdings Bhd's land in Kajang, Selangor was cancelled due to absence of bidders. Solicitors confirmed that the property, a piece of commercial land measuring about six acres, was not sold following the cancellation of the judicial auction via e-Lelong, the company said in an exchange filing. The land in Jalan Sinar Pagi was put up for auction at a reserve price of RM55.0m on Sept 21 under court order over an unpaid loan amid Country Heights' financial struggles after reporting losses over the last seven quarters. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The reserve price sets a ceiling, not a value, and it is the only number in the item. RM55.0m across about six acres is roughly RM9.2m an acre, or about RM210 a square foot on 261,360 sq ft - computed here. Because no bid was received, what the item actually establishes is that nobody would pay RM210 a square foot for this parcel on 21 September, which is a different statement from what the land is worth.

Today's edition contains a second land price and the contrast is worth stating carefully. Maybulk agreed to pay about RM395 a square foot for a Klang industrial property with buildings on it; Country Heights' Kajang commercial land found no bidder at about RM210 a square foot. Different land classes, different locations, one with buildings and one without, and one is a completed transaction while the other is a failed reserve. Both figures are computed here and the comparison is drawn here; it is not like-for-like.

The trigger is a court order over an unpaid loan, and every party to it is unnamed. No lender, no outstanding principal, no judgment sum, no charge details and no next auction date appears - so the shortfall this auction was meant to cover cannot be sized, and the item states no next step.

Seven consecutive quarters of losses is the only earnings datum, and it is given without figures. No revenue, no loss amount, no net gearing, no total borrowings and no other asset disposals are disclosed, so the auction cannot be placed within the company's overall financial position from the retrieved source.

This board holds no Kenanga coverage of Country Heights Holdings. Its Malaysian property coverage runs through SIMEPROP - named among Kenanga's top picks at OUTPERFORM with a RM2.10 target in the 3 September Market Strategy note - IOIPG (28 August), MAHSING (1 September), PARAMON (27 August) and ECOWLD (21 September), all developers of new product rather than holders of distressed land. The 23 September bundle carries no property report.

macro.h: South Korea confirms first project under USD350.0b US investment pact despite viability concerns
macro.body: South Korea confirmed its first project under a USD350.0b US investment pact on Tuesday and said it is considering two others, moving ahead despite profitability concerns and criticism from President Donald Trump over the pace of implementation. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: The pact is now named and it is far larger than the figure this board carried a fortnight ago. On 11 September the item was a Wall Street Journal report that South Korea was 'preparing to announce' a major US energy investment project worth more than USD100.0b aimed at AI build-out. Today the framing is a confirmed USD350.0b investment pact with its first project confirmed and two more under consideration - 3.5 times the earlier figure, and a bilateral pact rather than a single project. The digest connects the two nowhere; the sequence is assembled here, and the earlier report may or may not describe one project inside this pact.

The confirmed project is confirmed and nothing else. No name, no sector, no value, no US state, no counterparty and no timetable appears, and the two others are 'being considered'. So the headline figure is a programme ceiling while the only actual commitment disclosed is unsized.

The item concedes the objection in the same sentence as the announcement. Seoul is moving ahead 'despite profitability concerns' - the viability question is acknowledged, not quantified, with no return threshold, no financing structure and no risk-sharing arrangement described.

Political pressure on timing is named and runs one way. President Donald Trump has criticised the pace of implementation, which frames the confirmation as a response to an external deadline rather than a commercial decision. No deadline, no penalty and no renegotiation clause is stated.

There is no Malaysian read-across in the item and this board's nearest figure argues for caution in drawing one. Kenanga's 21 September External Trade note records August shipments to the United States at a record +139.1% YoY with electrical and electronic goods at 48.4% of total exports - Malaysia's US exposure is trade, not capital-account commitments between two third countries. The 23 September bundle is a single healthcare Company Update and carries no Kenanga view on Korea, US trade policy or cross-border investment.

macro.h: EU reaches initial free trade deal with Philippines in pivot to Asia
macro.body: The European Union (EU) and the Philippines have reached an initial free trade agreement as part of the bloc's broad pivot to Asia, Commissioner for Trade and Economic Security Maros Sefcovic said on Tuesday. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: 'Initial' is doing the work and nothing behind it is disclosed. No tariff schedule, no covered sectors, no rules of origin, no ratification timetable, no entry-into-force date and no bilateral trade value appears - so what was agreed on Tuesday cannot be distinguished from a political announcement in the retrieved source.

The competitive question for Malaysia is obvious in kind and unanswerable in figures. A fellow ASEAN exporter gaining preferential access to the EU market matters to the extent the two countries' export baskets overlap, and the item identifies not one product category on either side. This board holds no figure for Malaysia-EU trade and no status report on Malaysia's own EU negotiations.

The Philippines has appeared on this board once as a policy subject and in a different register: Kenanga's 28 August Philippines BSP Economic Viewpoint on a policy-rate increase, which recorded Manila among the Asian central banks that had tightened within the previous four months. Trade policy is a new angle on the same economy here.

It is the third distinct European workstream in three consecutive editions and none of the three connects to the others - the proposed EU windfall tax on energy companies (21 September), the ECB's blockchain settlement launch for tokenised wholesale transactions (22 September), and an FTA with a Southeast Asian economy today. Today's edition also carries a fourth, the UK's position on the EU's 'Made in Europe' plan.

No Malaysian listed company is named, no sector is identified, and the 23 September bundle carries no Economic Viewpoint, Market Strategy or sector report - so there is no Kenanga view in this edition on EU-ASEAN trade to weigh it against.

macro.h: Govt looking to strengthen R&D ecosystem, shift to 'Made by Malaysia' approach - Amir Hamzah
macro.body: The government is looking to strengthen Malaysia's research and development (R&D) ecosystem through more market-driven funding mechanisms and closer industry collaboration, said Minister of Finance II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Three instruments are named and none is sized: more market-driven funding mechanisms, closer industry collaboration, and a 'Made by Malaysia' framing. No R&D spending figure, no target share of GDP, no grant or tax-incentive change, no institution and no timeline appears, so nothing here can be measured against a later print.

The speaker and the timing are the informative part. This is the Minister of Finance II speaking sixteen days before Budget 2027 is tabled on 9 October 2026 - the tabling date is read from Kenanga's own Budget Preview, carried on this board yesterday, and the day count is computed here. Statements of this kind ahead of a budget are positioning rather than policy, and the item does not say whether any of it will appear in the budget.

It is consistent with Kenanga's reading of what Budget 2027 will be. Its Preview states outright that 'there is no revenue-reform pillar this year' and names growth priorities in AI, semiconductors and the digital economy; an R&D funding push sits on the spending and structural side of exactly that framing, not on the revenue side Kenanga says is missing.

'Made by Malaysia' is the second industrial-policy branding in today's macro bits, and the other is European. This edition also carries the UK's Andy Burnham wanting to work with the EU on its 'Made in Europe' plan - a scheme this board first recorded on 10 September as an EU push to direct more of its EUR2.6t of public contracts toward local suppliers, aimed at China. Two governments reaching for the same naming convention in one digest; the pairing is made here and neither item mentions the other.

No listed company is named and no sector allocation is given, and the 23 September bundle contains a single healthcare Company Update - so this edition carries no Kenanga economic publication to weigh it against. Kenanga's live 2026 GDP growth forecast on this board is 5.3%, most recently stated in its 21 September External Trade note.

macro.h: Malaysia to continue spending on development next year despite oil price pressures - Akmal Nasrullah
macro.body: Malaysia will keep spending on development in 2027 even as higher oil prices add pressure to the government's subsidy bill. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: This board already holds the number the statement is about, and it says the same thing. Kenanga's 22 September Budget 2027 Preview forecasts development expenditure rising to RM85.0b in 2027 from RM84.0b in 2026, while operating expenditure falls to RM364.0b from RM369.5b and net expenditure to RM448.0b from RM453.0b. Development spending is the one line Kenanga already has going up; the minister's statement is consistent with the house forecast rather than new information.

The oil-price pressure is also already quantified on this board, and it is Kenanga's own stated vulnerability. Its Preview runs on Brent averaging USD80/bbl in 2026 and USD74/bbl in 2027, with a footnote conceding the assumption is under review and will be revised higher, to about USD90 and USD80 - and this edition's commodity table shows Nymex crude at USD94.6/bbl on the 22 September session, down 1.24% from USD95.8, still above even the unpublished revision. Kenanga states that its fiscal arithmetic will be updated once the new oil view is finalised.

Higher oil is two-sided for Malaysia and the item gives only one side. It raises the subsidy bill, which is the pressure the minister addresses, and it also raises petroleum-related revenue, which the item does not mention. Kenanga's 2027 revenue forecast of RM365.0b, down from RM370.0b, is attributed specifically to a lower Brent assumption - so a higher oil price pushes that line the other way. The net fiscal effect is not established in either source, and that limitation is stated here rather than resolved.

No figure of any kind is attached to the commitment. No 2027 development allocation, no subsidy-bill estimate and no government oil-price assumption appears - 'will keep spending' is a direction, not an amount, and the amount is published on 9 October.

It is the first of two statements from Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah in this edition's four Malaysian macro bits, the other being on the quality of investment. The 23 September bundle carries no Economic Viewpoint, so Kenanga publishes no fiscal response to either today; its live position is the 22 September Preview, which puts the deficit at 3.8% of GDP in 2026 narrowing to 3.5% in 2027 on an unchanged -RM83.0b overall balance.

macro.h: Malaysia must prioritise investments that deliver better paying skilled jobs over numbers - minister
macro.body: Malaysia should look beyond the headline value of investments and focus on whether they create better-paying skilled jobs, raise productivity and strengthen local companies, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: Four quality tests are named and not one is measured: better-paying skilled jobs, higher productivity, stronger local companies, and looking beyond headline investment value. No wage target, no productivity figure, no approved-investment number, no sector and no timeline is attached, so a later edition has nothing precise to hold this against.

The headline measure being argued against is on this board with a figure. On 9 September it recorded the Selangor Menteri Besar's confidence that the state would exceed RM100.0b of investment value in 2026 - an approvals-style figure with no job, wage or productivity content attached, and recorded here at the time as exactly that. The minister is making the general case against the specific kind of number this board carried a fortnight ago; the connection is drawn here.

The labour market he is describing is quantified on this board and the tightness is real. Kenanga's 14 September Labour Market note has unemployment at 3.0% in July on 520.3k unemployed, labour force participation at a record 70.9% for a seventh consecutive month, and a 2026 unemployment forecast of 2.9%. Kenanga's own reading was that with participation flat at a record and the labour force growing 1.0% YoY, further falls in unemployment must come from employment outgrowing the labour force.

That makes this a price argument about a market where the quantity argument is close to exhausted. If participation is at a record and unemployment near 3%, additional headline investment volume competes for a labour pool that is barely growing, and what is left to improve is what each job pays. That reading is drawn here; neither the item nor Kenanga's note states it.

Both Malaysian statements in this edition come from the same minister and they are different arguments - one about the state's own development spending, one about the investment it attracts. No listed company is named in either, and the 23 September bundle carries no Economic Viewpoint, Market Strategy or sector note that would take a Kenanga position on investment quality.

macro.h: Malaysia to grow 4.7% in 2026 as Southeast Asian outlook brightens - World Economic Forum
macro.body: Malaysia's economy is projected to grow 4.7% in 2026, supported by technology-related exports and investment as well as robust domestic demand, according to the World Economic Forum (WEF). (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: This is the clearest third-party disagreement with Kenanga's house view this board has carried. The WEF projects 4.7% growth for Malaysia in 2026; Kenanga's forecast is 5.3% (2025: 5.2%), maintained as recently as its 21 September External Trade note and restated in the 14 September Labour Market and Distributive Trade notes. A 0.6 percentage point gap, computed here, and nothing in either source reconciles them.

The two agree on composition and disagree only on magnitude, which is what makes the gap interesting. The WEF's stated drivers - technology-related exports, investment and robust domestic demand - are the same three Kenanga has been using all month. A shared diagnosis producing different numbers points to different assumptions about pace rather than about the shape of the economy; that inference is drawn here.

Kenanga's 2026 evidence has been running strong, not soft, which makes the WEF the more conservative of the two. Its 21 September note has August exports up 45.5% YoY with the trade surplus widening to RM28.1b, the 2026 export forecast raised to 28.5% from 19.0%, and exports on track to exceed RM2.0 trillion - while cautioning that both exports and imports fell month-on-month and that growth should slow in 2H26 as base effects fade. That caution is the part of Kenanga's own note closest to the WEF's number.

The regional claim in the headline cannot be tested from the item. 'As Southeast Asian outlook brightens' comes with no comparison figure for any other ASEAN economy, no 2027 projection, no quarterly path and no prior WEF forecast for Malaysia, so neither the level nor the direction of revision is establishable.

The 23 September bundle contains one report, an IHH Healthcare Company Update, so Kenanga publishes no response to this in today's edition. This is a forecast that a later edition can test against an actual print, which distinguishes it from most of the unquantified policy items around it.

macro.h: Thailand's cabinet approves USD1.29b consumer subsidy extension
macro.body: Thailand's cabinet has agreed to spend 43 billion baht (USD1.29 billion) to extend a consumer subsidy scheme for another two months to help ease living costs, the finance minister said on Tuesday. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: It is the follow-through on yesterday's item and it went the other way. On 22 September this board carried Finance Minister Ekniti Nitithanprapas saying Thailand was considering an excise tax cut on fuel - giving up revenue. Today the same minister announces a cabinet-approved spending measure instead: THB43b over two months. Whether the tax cut is still live is not stated in either source, and the two items make no reference to one another; the sequence is assembled here.

The stated pair of figures implies an exchange rate the item does not print: THB43b at USD1.29b is about 33.3 baht to the dollar, computed here. On the same arithmetic the measure runs at about THB21.5b a month, which is the figure an extension beyond two months would repeat.

'Extension' is the operative word and the item gives no baseline. No original scheme size, no start date, no eligibility criteria, no product scope and no end date beyond the two months appears - so the cumulative cost of the programme cannot be established, only this tranche.

It is now the fourth distinct policy response to the same energy shock this board has recorded inside a week, and the four occupy different points on the same value chain. Malaysia widened a consumer subsidy, with BUDI95's quota restored to 300 litres from 1 September - sized by Kenanga's Budget Preview at RM0.5b to RM1.0b over September to December, some 2 to 5 basis points of GDP. Malaysia also had its listed utility absorb an electricity cost, with TENAGA taking RM120m to RM150m (21 September). Europe proposed taxing energy producers (21 September). Thailand floated a tax cut and has now approved a subsidy - both sides of the ledger in two days.

Thailand already runs the loosest policy rate in Kenanga's own table of thirteen, at 1.00%, recorded here on 21 September from its BoJ Economic Viewpoint, against Malaysia's OPR of 2.75% held for fourteen months. A fiscal transfer of this size on top of that is a second easing lever, not a first. No report in the 23 September bundle carries a Kenanga view on Thailand.

macro.h: Fed's Collins says rate hike will help reach inflation goal
macro.body: Federal Reserve Bank of Boston President Susan Collins said she supported last week's decision to raise interest rates, which she said would help bring inflation back to the central bank's 2% target. (Bloomberg)
takeaways: The content is an endorsement rather than news, and nothing measurable is attached. Collins 'supported' the decision and says it 'would help bring inflation back to the central bank's 2% target' - no rate path, no inflation forecast, no meeting reference and no time frame. The hike was unanimous at 12-0, per Kenanga's own 17 September FOMC note, so her vote for it was already on the record. It is also the only Bloomberg-sourced item in today's macro bits.

It is the second consecutive edition carrying an FOMC participant defending the September hike, and the two make different arguments. Goolsbee, carried yesterday, conceded the cost - the road to 2% 'may not be painless'. Collins asserts the efficacy - that the hike will help get there. One is about what it will take, the other about whether it works.

Efficacy is precisely the point Kenanga disputes. This board recorded on 17 September that Kenanga called the September hike a policy error on the grounds that the inflation impulse is an energy and geopolitical shock that a higher funds rate cannot supply into. Collins's claim does not engage that objection in the retrieved item, so the disagreement stands unaddressed rather than resolved.

What matters for Kenanga's live position is not September but what follows it. Its 21 September Bond Market Weekly Outlook states a base case that the latest Fed hike 'marks the end of the tightening cycle', with policy rates unchanged through end-2027, and its 17 September note leans to one-and-done at 3.75%-4.00%. Two sitting participants publicly justifying the hike in two days is consistent with that call only if neither is arguing for the next one - and neither, on the retrieved text, is.

The market did not trade it either way and no causal link should be read into that. This edition's tables show the Dow down 0.36% to 51,863.7, the S&P 500 unchanged at 7,764.6 and the NASDAQ up 0.45% to 27,244.3 on the 22 September session, with USD/MYR at 4.0752 from 4.0778. It is context, not a response.

macro.h: UK's Burnham wants to work with EU on 'Made in Europe' plan
macro.body: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he would argue for Britain to be a 'trusted partner' to the European Union's (EU) 'Made in Europe' scheme, saying they should not be pitted as enemies on a policy that has the potential to hammer the UK's car industry. (The Edge Malaysia)
takeaways: This board holds the scheme he is responding to. On 10 September it carried the EU pushing governments to direct more of their EUR2.6t of public contracts toward local suppliers under 'Made in Europe', explicitly aimed at China. Today a non-member asks to be treated as inside it. The two items are thirteen days apart and neither references the other; the link is made here.

The stated exposure is one industry and it is not sized. The policy 'has the potential to hammer the UK's car industry' - with no tariff rate, no local-content threshold, no affected volume, no timeline and no estimate of contracts at risk. 'Trusted partner' is a requested status, not an agreed one.

This board has carried the UK's car industry as a weakening one already: British vehicle production fell 11.6% YoY in July on weaker exports and summer shutdowns, recorded here on 28 August. A procurement rule that excluded UK content would land on a sector already contracting, which is the practical content of the warning; the connection is drawn here.

It is the second industrial-policy branding in today's digest, beside Malaysia's 'Made by Malaysia' R&D framing, and the third European entry in three editions after the proposed EU windfall tax (21 September) and the ECB's blockchain settlement launch (22 September). This is the first of the European run that is about market access rather than energy or monetary policy.

There is no Malaysian read-across and none is claimed. This board's automotive coverage is domestic-demand work - Kenanga's 21 September Automotive Sector Update, BAUTO (11 September) and MBMR (2 September) - and a European content rule does not reach any of them. The 23 September bundle carries no European or automotive report; its single publication is a healthcare Company Update.

reports.flag: Six points of caution on this row, reported as printed rather than resolved. (1) The sum-of-parts does not divide to the stated target price. Page 3 prints hospitals at RM84,210m, Fortis at RM5,320.2m, the 32.9% Plife REIT stake at RM1,943.4m and net debt of -RM11,416.0m, which sum to exactly the RM80,057m total shown. Divided by the 8,836m shares in the same table that is RM9.06, not the RM9.10 target stated on page 1 and in the peer table - a gap of about 0.4%, computed here. The note states there is no ESG adjustment on a 3-star rating, so nothing in the document bridges the two. The RM9.10 Kenanga states is what this row carries. (2) Singapore bed occupancy is given three different ways in one document. The investment case says occupancy recovered 'to above 52% in August and September'; the highlights box says 'to 55% in July and August (against 51% in 2QFY26)'; the Singapore section says 'to >52% in Aug-Sept (vs. 51% in 2QFY26 and 49% in 1QFY26)'. Different levels over different months, unreconciled. (3) The retracement that justifies the upgrade is stated as 10% while the note's own header prints YTD stock price change of -8.6%. Both appear on page 1. (4) A table row is mislabelled. The Türkiye table's row 'Türkiye Operations foreign patient revenue as a % of Turkiye and Europe revenue' prints 18%/15%/14%/13%/11% - but those figures divide foreign patient revenue by Türkiye Operations revenue, not by Türkiye and Europe revenue (FY23: 754/4,189 = 18%; 1H26: 408/3,712 = 11%). Against the regional total, 1H26 would be 8.6%. Arithmetic here; the prose repeats the label, describing medical tourism as a percentage of 'total regional revenue'. (5) The growth block on page 4 labelled 'Net Profit /(loss)' tracks core net profit, not reported net profit. It prints 32%/8%/22%/9% for FY2024A-FY2027F, which are the growth rates of the core series (1,685/1,818/2,216/2,409); the reported series (2,657/2,101/2,216/2,409) grows -20.9%/+5.5%/+8.7% over the same years. Computed here. (6) The peer table's Rating column returned no values in the retrieved text layer, so no peer ratings are used on this row; the target prices in that table were readable and do reconcile with this board's record.
reports.name: IHH Healthcare Berhad
reports.catalyst: An upgrade with no new financial results behind it. Following a meeting with IHH's Investor Relations, Kenanga upgrades the stock to OUTPERFORM from MARKET PERFORM and lifts its sum-of-parts target price to RM9.10 from RM8.50, calling the YTD share price retracement a compelling entry point for a global healthcare operator with positions in four core regions. FY26F and FY27F net profit are each raised 6%, driven entirely by a cut to the forecast Greater China loss - FY27F now RM129m against RM250m previously - after losses there halved in 1HFY26 on bottom-line profitability at the 500-bed Gleneagles Hong Kong Hospital, which has now posted six consecutive months of net profit. The target-price increase also reflects a revised valuation of the 31%-owned Fortis Healthcare stake, taken at a 40% discount to market value (an implied 21x EV/EBITDA at the lower end of its historical five-year average) to account for the ongoing forensic audit ordered by the Delhi High Court, which Kenanga notes imposes no liability, penalty or fine on either IHH or Fortis. Singapore bed occupancy has recovered from 1QFY26 lows, Türkiye and Europe are expected to outpace 1HFY26 in the second half on price catch-ups and newly consolidated hospitals, and Gleneagles India's margins are expected to converge with Fortis's under the Master Services Agreement. No ESG adjustment on a 3-star rating.
reports.quote: Following a meeting with IHH's Investor Relations, we upgrade the stock to OUTPERFORM from MARKET PERFORM.
summary: What moved, checked against this board's own record and against this edition's tables. Both the rating and the target price moved, and both previous values reconcile exactly: this board read IHH at MARKET PERFORM with a RM8.50 target from its own 28 August Results Note PDF, which are the precise figures this note upgrades from. The share price of RM8.00 matches this edition's own tables, where IHH is the top gainer at +5.0% on 6.22m shares, and the KLCI of 1,683.50 printed in the report matches the 1,683.5 in the digest. The upside to target is 13.8% (9.10/8.00), which matches the peer table, and adding the 1.4% FY26F net dividend yield gives about 15.2% of expected total return - clearing the 'more than 10%' OUTPERFORM threshold defined on page 7. Both computed here; the note shows neither step. Forecasts move in one direction only: FY26F and FY27F net profit each +6%, to RM2,215.9m and RM2,408.8m.

The target price arithmetic, and the one place it does not close. The sum-of-parts is built from hospitals excluding listed companies at RM84,210m on 14.5x EV/EBITDA - itself a 40% historical discount to ASEAN and Indian players - plus RM5,320.2m for Fortis at a 40% discount to market value, plus RM1,943.4m for the 32.9% Plife REIT stake at a 30% discount, less RM11,416.0m of net debt. Those four sum to exactly the RM80,057m total printed. Divided by the 8,836m shares in the same table that is RM9.06, not the RM9.10 stated, and the note explicitly makes no ESG adjustment on its 3-star rating - so nothing in the document bridges the 0.4% gap. Arithmetic here; see the flag. The implied FY27F EV/EBITDA at the target is 15x, against 13.4x at the RM8.00 share price.

The upgrade is Greater China plus the minority line, not an improving operating trajectory - and that is visible in Kenanga's own table. FY26F EBITDA is forecast flat at RM5,618m, operating profit falls 10% to RM3,872m and PBT falls 13% to RM2,992m, yet core net profit rises 22% to RM2,215.9m. The bridge is below the operating line: tax falls to RM606m from RM821m as the effective rate drops to 20% from 24%, and minority interest falls to RM170m from RM506m - a RM336m swing the note nowhere explains. All computed here. On Greater China itself, the FY27F loss forecast is cut to RM129m from RM250m, but 1HFY26's net loss of RM56m (1HFY25: RM90m) annualises to about RM112m, so even the reduced forecast assumes losses wider than the current run-rate - also arithmetic here. Kenanga sits below the consensus it prints, by 2.6% for FY26F (RM2,215.9m against RM2,274m) and 8.6% for FY27F (RM2,408.8m against RM2,635m).

The regional detail, including one table that does not measure what its label says. Singapore: 2QFY26 EBITDA margin expanded to 29% from 26% in 1QFY26 on occupancy recovering from 1Q lows, with an explicit 'tactical pivot' to an out-of-hospital ambulatory model to move low-acuity cases off inpatient beds. Malaysia: 2QFY26 EBITDA margin 28% (1QFY26: 26%) on bed occupancy of 64% (59%), with daycare revenue +13% YoY to RM286m, or 11% of Malaysia revenue. Türkiye and Europe: revenue per inpatient admission +22% YoY in 2QFY26, regional EBITDA +35% YoY, 2QFY26 margin 20% against 21% in 1QFY26, and a long-term group EBITDA margin target of 23%. Türkiye foreign patient revenue was RM408m in 1H26, +4% YoY - which is 11% of Türkiye Operations revenue of RM3,712m, not of the RM4,721m regional total the table's own row label claims; computed here, and flagged. India: Fortis now manages five of the six Gleneagles India hospitals under the MSA/O&M structure, targeting Gleneagles India EBITDA margins of 18%-19% from about 10%, with consolidated India at 18% in 2QFY26 and 19% in 1HFY26 against a 25% target.

Why the Kenanga Signal reads None stated while the Analyst Signal reads Positive, and a peer table that agrees with this board four times out of four. The investment case reads 'We like IHH for: (i) its pricing power, as the inelastic demand for healthcare provides it with the ability to pass cost through amidst rising inflation, (ii) the strong recovery in patient throughput, from both domestic and international markets, and (iii) its commanding market position in the private healthcare space'. Searching all seven pages for this board's full conviction list returns only that construction, plus 'favourable second-half seasonality' - and nothing for top pick, sector pick, our pick, preferred, most attractive, favour or favourite. This board treats 'we like' as investment-case language rather than a pick declaration, the same treatment given GAMUDA on 22 September, TENAGA on 21 September, KEYFIELD on 18 September and MISC on 17 September, so the Kenanga Signal reads None stated. Kenanga's declared healthcare sector Top Pick on this board remains DUOPHARMA, from its 28 August note - 'remains our Top Pick for the healthcare sector' - and today's peer table prints DUOPHARMA at RM1.72, the same target this board read from that PDF. So do the other three covered peers this board holds: KPJ at RM3.05 (9 September), KOTRA at RM3.88 (28 August) and SCOMNET at RM0.570 (24 August). Separately, this is the second healthcare upgrade in a fortnight on the identical mechanism - KPJ was upgraded to OUTPERFORM on 9 September after a 19% share-price retracement with its target unchanged; IHH is upgraded today after a retracement, with the target raised.

analyst.note: The Analyst Signal reads Positive on CIMB Securities, and the date gap has to be stated up front: the call is dated 28 July 2026, fifty-seven days before the Kenanga note beside it. Reported by The Star on that date, CIMB Research maintained an 'overweight' call on healthcare stocks 'with top picks being IHH Healthcare Bhd and KPJ Healthcare Bhd, both with "buy" calls and a "hold" on Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd', and kept a target price of RM10.30 on IHH. That is a named house, a dated note and explicit pick language, which is what §3 requires; no more recent CIMB statement on IHH was retrievable in this run, so under the most-recent-statement rule it stands. The most recent named-house call on IHH is a different house and carries no pick language. The Edge Malaysia reported on 22 September 2026 - the session immediately before this Kenanga note - that Macquarie retained IHH on 'outperform' and raised its target price to RM11.10, 'one of the highest out of 26 analysts tracked by Bloomberg', on the argument that at 12 times consensus forward enterprise valuation the stock trades near the lower end of its regional peers and close to historical lows. That note is the identified cause of the 5% rally that produced the RM8.00 share price Kenanga calls a compelling entry point - a point neither document makes, and one worth holding alongside the upgrade. One further dated pick stands, older. The Edge Malaysia reported on 13 January 2026 that Hong Leong Investment Bank maintained 'overweight' on healthcare with top picks IHH at RM9.43 and KPJ at RM3.16. The divergence flag is not set: CIMB's buy at RM10.30, Macquarie's outperform at RM11.10 and HLIB's buy at RM9.43 all sit on the same side as Kenanga's OUTPERFORM at RM9.10, and all three targets are above it. Two earlier CIMB notes are recorded and not used as data - a 13 May 2026 earnings preview raising the target 30 sen to RM10.30 with a 'buy', which is where the RM10.30 originates, and a 26 September 2025 note calling IHH its top sector pick at a RM8.50 target, superseded on both the pick and the price. Two further calls surfaced in search and are deliberately not used. A reported Maybank Investment Bank 'preferred large-cap' listing of IHH at RM11.17, attributed to The Star of 4 July 2026, could not be read: the page returned only navigation and subscription markup on every attempt. A reported RHB target-price raise to RM9.52 dated February 2026, attributed to the New Straits Times, returned only navigation markup as well. The contents of those pages are not used. Of the nine houses this board searches, two yielded a dated, publicly retrievable call read in full during this run - CIMB Securities and Hong Leong Investment Bank. Maybank Investment Bank, RHB Investment Bank, AmInvestment Bank Research, Public Investment Bank, TA Securities, MIDF and Affin Hwang did not. Positive here means pick language was found in an accessible, dated, named-house source - not that the street is unanimous; equally, the absence of a call from seven houses means nothing was retrievable, not that they hold no view.
